court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Roshan S/O Suryakant Raghtate vs Mrs. Poonam W/O Roshan Raghtate
facts_of_case: The husband filed a petition for divorce on grounds of cruelty and desertion. The wife left the matrimonial home within 15 days of marriage and started residing with her mother. The husband served notices to the wife but she did not reply.

legal_principles.principle: A complaint filed after a long delay may raise doubts about its genuineness.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted that the wife not only filed the complaint for an offence punishable under the provisions of Section 498-A of the Penal Code read with Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act against the husband and his family members but she filed the complaint at the time when the brother of the husband was getting married.
use_in: divorce cases where delay in filing complaint is an issue

legal_principles.principle: A party's failure to file a reply to notices may be considered as desertion.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted that the wife had not filed the reply to the notices sent by the husband dated 09.09.2008 and 21.01.2009.
use_in: divorce cases where failure to file reply is an issue

outcome.final_order: The trial court's decision dismissing the petition for divorce was upheld.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act
advising on grounds for divorce in Indian courts
